verdict: APPROVE the bounded PIO/power ownership layer for host and fake-MMIO stages. No blockers. Seven non-blocking items below; R1-R3 are worth fixing before the first hardware run.

tests.astra: test_adapter.py: 17/17 pass here (cc -Wall -Wextra -Werror, UBSan). Includes validation of the board guard against the real saved ADT.
tests.independent: Scratch harness (not in repo) with its own fake PMGR/GPIO/SPI model: happy path, read gated on NUB13, write plus status, bad status, SPI3 never on, SPI3 DEV_DISABLE, SIO off, pin LOCK, WORD_DELAY nonzero, and an MMIO-fault injection at each of 400 access indices. 0 SPI accesses before SPI3 reads 0xf, 0 parent writes, and every error left the adapter faulted.

verified: No SPI3 read or write before SPI3 reads target=actual=0xf: power() succeeds only through (v&0xff)==0xff or a polled actual 0xf with BUSY clear (pio.c:54-87). spi_access and controller() come after.
SIO_BUSIF, SIO and NUB_GPIO are only read and verified, never written, reset or powered down on any path. This fits m1n1, which hooks and shadows SIO and SIO_BUSIF (hv/__init__.py:1473-1514).
All six pins are read and LOCK-checked before any GPIO write (pio.c:93-97). The writes match the pinned Linux ops: pinmux_set :187-188, direction_input :243-246, direction_output :256-258.

Controller setup equals spi-apple.c init/prep_transfer: CFG=0x20, PIN CS high, OVERRIDE_CS clear, PINCFG KEEP_CS, FIFO reset, delays 0, CLKDIV 15, BITS 8. Every offset and bit matches the pinned header.

The FIFO level is bounded before each RXDATA read (pio.c:193), which avoids the reference overflow at spi-apple.c:432-437. One 200 ms deadline plus an iteration cap per transaction. CS timing is 65 us setup, 200 us write/status gap, 65 us hold, 250 us idle.

Reads happen only while NUB13 is low (pio.c:235-242). A status mismatch fails the write. Faults idle the controller, raise CS, drive spien low and latch faulted. Stop is idempotent and records cleanup failures.
m1n1 maps all arm-io ranges as passthrough (hv/__init__.py:1400-1403). Only the UART/USB PMGR chains, the vuart and two PMGR overrides are hooked, so SPI3, GPIO and nub-gpio accesses are not trapped.

items.issue: (!rx && rl) fails every write if the controller fills the RX FIFO while RXCNT=0. Linux never reads RX in TX-only transfers and only resets the FIFO before the next one, so this hardware behavior is unproven either way. It fails closed, but reports the same M1KBD_FIFO code as real FIFO errors.
items.fix: Use a distinct result code, or drain and discard up to 16 bytes, so the first hardware run can tell the two apart.

items.issue: A single BUSY sample refuses start. BUSY is a transient hardware bit, especially on auto-PM domains such as GPIO.
items.fix: Re-sample for up to 100 us before refusing.

items.issue: SPI3 is written read-modify-write from power_before[3], which was sampled before SPI_P and GPIO were activated.
items.fix: Re-read SPI3 immediately before writing it.

items.issue: A shared domain found with target 0xf, AUTO set and actual clock-gated gets AUTO cleared and is held fully on. Functionally harmless, but it is not 'kept as found'.
items.fix: Accept target 0xf with AUTO set as usable without writing, or document the change.

items.issue: spi_access is set before pins(), so a pin-lock refusal still writes SPI CTRL/IE/PIN during cleanup (4 writes in the harness). Safe, because power is on.

One status mismatch powers the keyboard off and faults the adapter. Right for the diagnostic stages; a long-running driver may want to report the failed write and keep power, still with no broad retry.

The 5, 5 and 50 ms waits must sleep (IOSleep on a workloop), not spin with IODelay. now_us must be monotonic. ADAPTER.md is referenced by the headers but absent from this snapshot. Pins are changed and not restored on stop, and SPI3 is left powered on.
